Explain in your own words what 'Extrachromosomal Maternal Inheritance' refers to.
questions.a: Plastids and mitochondria carry their own DNA, and because the sperm sheds its cytoplasm at fertilisation, these organellar genomes pass down the maternal line alone; the white, green and variegated leaves of the four-o'clock plant demonstrated that cytoplasmic traits follow the mother's phenotype rather than Mendel's rules.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Extrachromosomal Maternal Inheritance'.
questions.a: No paternal contribution reaches plastids or mitochondria, so offspring mirror the mother's cytoplasmic genotype.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Extrachromosomal Maternal Inheritance' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'Forward and Reverse Genetics' refers to.
questions.a: Two research directions bracket the gene: forward genetics starts from visible or molecular phenotypic variation and hunts for the DNA behind it, while reverse genetics begins with a sequenced gene or protein of unknown job, silences or disrupts it - say by RNA interference - and reads the resulting phenotype to deduce its function.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Forward and Reverse Genetics'.
questions.a: Phenotype-to-gene is forward; gene-to-phenotype is reverse, with RNAi or targeted disruption as the probe.
